group_assessment.weighting: An Egyptian paediatric neurology service reporting two cases; descriptive clinical. Not a WWOX group and not a primary group for any WWOX phenotype: the paper is a SUBSTITUTE for the folate axis, class level only, not WWOX evidence. Observation (imaging, exome result) weighed above the stated treatment benefit, which is unquantified.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (substitute, disease class). In both children the diagnosis of cerebral folate transport deficiency rests on exome sequencing and imaging; CSF 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, the defining analyte, was not measured.
entries.snippet: Unfortunately, we could not measure the levels of CSF MTHF as the test is not present in our country.

experimental_context.system: two unrelated children with biallelic FOLR1 variants (class level: cerebral folate transport deficiency); NOT a WWOX system
experimental_context.genotype: homozygous FOLR1 loss-of-function class; no WWOX

entries.proposition: The first child's variant is called a 'homozygous nonsense pathogenic variant' while the protein change given, p.R128W, is a missense substitution.
entries.snippet: revealing homozygous nonsense pathogenic variant in FOLR1 gene in exon 3 c.C382T p.R128W, which confirms the diagnosis of cerebral folate deficiency.

entries.proposition: The routine metabolic screen in the first child (ammonia, lactate, acylcarnitine profile, urine organic acids; CSF glucose, protein, lactate) was normal, i.e. in this child a normal routine metabolic screen coexisted with genetically confirmed FOLR1 deficiency (the authors draw no wider inference).
entries.snippet: Laboratory investigations as blood ammonia, serum lactate, acyl carnitine profile in blood, and urine organic acid, were done with normal results.

entries.proposition: The treatment response is given as better-controlled seizures with no counts, no repeat EEG and no CSF folate recheck; complete control was not reached.
entries.snippet: At this dose of folinic acid, seizures became better controlled (less frequent and less duration).

entries.proposition: The statement that folic acid is contraindicated in this condition (it competes for the receptor) is a restatement with one citation (reference 6, Al-Baradie, 'Diagnosis and management of cerebral folate deficiency'; the source does not label it a review); class-level and not advice.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, folic acid is contraindicated in these conditions as it competitively binds to FRα, further reducing 5-MTHF transport into the brain.6
